decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Lucy' in turn 7, explicitly naming B.
A's question 'what does your friend do?' in turn 15 presupposes B has a friend.

decisions.claim: B is associated with a male person referred to as 'him'
decisions.reason: A asks 'When can I see him?' in turn 9, presupposing B knows who 'him' is and can facilitate the meeting, implying association.
decisions.counterexample: 'him' could be a mutual acquaintance rather than B's own associate, but B must know who is referenced.

decisions.claim: B proposed something that A accepted
decisions.reason: 'That will be fine' in turn 9 presupposes B proposed or suggested something that A is accepting.

decisions.claim: B is associated with a male person ('him') that A wants to see
decisions.reason: c5 is essentially the same claim as c3 (B is associated with 'him' that A wants to see), just with slightly different wording. c3 is the more general and complete representative.

decisions.claim: B will travel by bus to meet A
decisions.reason: 'By bus, of course' in turn 13 is A's own statement about how A will travel (to pick up friend at airport), not about B's mode of travel. This is an A-as-B attribution error.
decisions.counterexample: A is explaining how A will get to the airport, not how B will come to A.

decisions.claim: B has a friend whose occupation A is curious about
decisions.reason: c7 adds the detail about A's curiosity regarding occupation, but the core fact 'B has a friend' is identical to c2. The curiosity is A's state, not B's attribute.

decisions.claim: B and A have agreed to meet at a specific time
decisions.reason: 'Ok, see you then' in turn 17 presupposes a mutual agreement on a meeting time was reached in the unseen B turn.

decisions.claim: B must come to A's location before noon to meet
decisions.reason: A explicitly instructs B in turn 11: 'Make sure you come here before noon.' This is a direct statement about B's required action.

decisions.claim: B is expected to arrive before A picks up a friend at the airport in the afternoon
decisions.reason: c10 is a causal elaboration of c9 (the reason B must come before noon). The core fact about B's obligation is the same; c9 is the more direct representative.
